intro: You are standing before Hagia Irene, a monastery and church in İstanbul province from the 4th century AD. This was the city's first church, and in 381 the Second Ecumenical Council met here. Because it was never converted into a mosque, its interior survives as it was.
history: The city's first church was built under Constantine, and in 381 the Second Ecumenical Council gathered within it. In the Nika revolt of 532 it burned, and Justinian rebuilt it. So what kept it unchanged? After the conquest it stood inside the first court of Topkapı Palace, so it was never converted into a mosque, and its interior survives as it was.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the mosaic cross in the apse and the synthronon, then the atrium and the domed nave.
facts: Did you know? The plain mosaic cross in the apse dates from iconoclasm: a cross was set there in place of any figure. This is the city's first church, and the Second Ecumenical Council met in it in 381. Because it was never converted into a mosque, its interior survives as it was, plain cross in the apse included.
outro: This brings our tour of Hagia Irene to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for sharing these quiet walls with us, and enjoy your visit.
